RICO — The Legal Framework

Michigan RICO — MCL 750.159i

“A person employed by, or associated with, an enterprise shall not conduct or participate in the affairs of the enterprise directly or indirectly through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements required:

  1. An enterprise — any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or group of individuals associated in fact (MCL 750.159f(a))
  2. Employment or association with the enterprise
  3. Conduct or participation in the enterprise’s affairs
  4. Through a pattern of racketeering activity — at least 2 incidents of racketeering activity, one of which occurred within 5 years of the other (MCL 750.159f(c))

Penalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment (MCL 750.159i)

Federal RICO — 18 U.S.C. § 1962

“It shall be unlawful for any person employed by or associated with any enterprise engaged in, or the activities of which affect, interstate or foreign commerce, to conduct or participate, directly or indirectly, in the conduct of such enterprise’s affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements: Same core structure. Federal RICO adds mail fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1341), wire fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1343), and money laundering (18 U.S.C. § 1956) as predicates.

Penalty: Up to 20 years per count, plus forfeiture.

What This Page Is

Brian Banks wrote a book. He named people. He described relationships. He confessed to behaviors — his own and others’. Every word is a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — his own published statement, admissible against him in pending litigation.

This page catalogs every person named in the book, identifies who they are using public records, and documents the relationships and behaviors Banks described in his own words.

Fair use notice: All excerpts are used for criticism, commentary, and public-interest reporting under 17 U.S.C. § 107. See the companion analysis for the full fair use framework.

The Judges — Three “Mentors” Who Are Sitting or Retired Jurists

Judge Denise Langford Morris — 42 References

Role per Banks: “my mentor” Actual role: Banks’s felony sentencing judge in Oakland County Circuit Court (~1999). Now retired. Wrote the book’s foreword.

Banks describes a relationship that progressed from judge-defendant to personal mentorship to campaign labor to credential endorsement:

  1. Sentenced Banks leniently (1-year probation, 6 months tether)
  2. Told Banks: “you need to get back in school and go to someone’s law school!” — while knowing his felonies would bar admission
  3. Met Banks for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac through mutual friend Roeiah
  4. Discussed her morning docket with civilians at the restaurant: Banks writes that “Judge Langford Morris was describing her morning docket to Roeiah and the other young lady and the various cases that she had heard.” A sitting judge describing active cases she heard that morning to non-lawyers at a restaurant.
  5. Invited Banks back to her courtroom and paraded him to staff
  6. Attended MSU Law BLSA events at Banks’s invitation
  7. Treated Banks to dinner when he “graduated from law school” — along with “several other judges”
  8. Banks volunteered on her Michigan Supreme Court campaign
  9. Wrote the foreword to a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.” — endorsing the credential fraud of the felon she sentenced

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Discussed active cases with civilians in a restaurant (Canon 2, Rule 2.10 — Judicial Statements on Pending Cases)
  • Developed a personal ex parte relationship with a former defendant
  • Used a former felon defendant for campaign labor
  • Endorsed credential fraud in a published book foreword
📄 Documented

Judge Vonda Evans — 9+ References

Role per Banks: “my mentor,” campaign strategist, friend Actual role: Retired Wayne County Circuit Court judge

Banks writes: “Retired Judge Vonda Evans and I became friends almost sixteen years ago. Vonda and I met through a mutual attorney friend one summer while hanging out in downtown Detroit.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Coined “Bank on Banks” — the campaign slogan: “After going back and forth with several ideas, Vonda finally said, ‘I got it! Bank on Banks!’”
  • Provided campaign strategy advice for a nine-time convicted felon running for office
  • Arrived at Banks’s grandfather’s hospital with Judge Cylenthia Miller — demonstrating personal, not professional, relationship
  • Was present the night before the grandfather’s death alongside Gay-Dagnogo
  • Banks describes her as “the queen of unorthodox campaigning” who “would unintentionally campaign even when her elections were years away”
📄 Documented

Role per Banks: “my mentor,” “like family,” “big sister” Actual role: Sitting 3rd Circuit Court Judge. PCA Board President (LARA Entity 900072324). JTC complaint filed.

Banks writes: “She was a mentor for me while I was in law school and eventually became like family. We’ve watched each other grow and take prominent roles in the political world. From a district court judge to now a circuit court judge, I’ve been with her every step of the way.”

And: “my big sister, Cylenthia, and I survived.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Arrived at Banks’s grandfather’s hospital alongside Judge Vonda Evans — personal family crisis response by sitting judges
  • Maintained a “like family” relationship with a nine-time convicted felon while serving as a judge
  • Currently serves as Board President of a school operated by that same convicted felon
  • Banks’s description of watching “each other grow and take prominent roles” implies mutual support throughout both careers
📄 Documented

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend in acknowledgments Actual role: Wayne County judge

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend in acknowledgments Actual role: Wayne County judge

The Inner Circle — Domestic and Economic Unit

Role per Banks: “my best friend and brother… You’ve now become a permanent fixture in our family” Actual role: Three-time convicted felon. PAC treasurer (Bank on Banks PAC). Shares Banks’s mailing address. Domestic/economic partner.

Banks describes Holland at every major life event:

  • First call when the FBI arrived: “I called Joe, who was at work, and told him what had just taken place and asked him to meet me at the lawyer’s office at 11 a.m.”

This is not a business relationship. This is a domestic/economic unit described in the defendant’s own published words.

Roeiah is the connective tissue of the entire Banks-judiciary relationship:

A sitting judge who Banks states had “felonies and misdemeanors” and “spent a month or two in jail.” Banks published this. It’s his party admission about a member of his network. Her sister operates his school. They still live one street apart.

Lens: 🕸️ Topology ⚛️ Lattice 📅 Chronology 💰 Money ⚖️ Legal 🏛️ Capture

The Physics

In 1958, physicist Philip W. Anderson showed that disorder in a crystal lattice prevents electrons from propagating. Instead of flowing through the material, electrons become trapped — localized — near the defect sites. The stronger the disorder, the shorter the distance an electron can travel before it stops.

This is not a metaphor. It is a mathematical identity.

Replace lattice sites with court divisions. Replace electrons with cases. Replace disorder potential with captured judges. The same equation applies: cases entering a disordered judicial system cannot propagate to a fair hearing. They localize.

The Lattice

Rendered by petalTongue — heatmap, bar chart, and faceted gauges via the grammar-of-graphics scene compiler.

The Measurement: Localization Length (ξ)

In physics, the localization length ξ measures how far an electron can travel through a disordered lattice before it becomes trapped. The formula:

ξ = −1 / ln(1 − p)

Where p is the probability of encountering a captured judge on any given bench that handles that case type.

  • ξ < 5 → Strongly localized. A case has almost no chance of receiving an independent hearing.
  • 5 ≤ ξ < 10 → Moderately localized. Some paths exist, but most lead through captured benches.
  • ξ > 10 → Weakly localized. Capture exists but is diluted across enough judges.

What the Numbers Mean

Probate: The Deepest Trap (ξ = 3.5)

Wayne County Probate has 4 judges. One of them — David Perkins — is Chief Judge Pro Tem, meaning he has case assignment authority. He decides which judge hears which probate, guardianship, conservatorship, and estate case.

A 25% random capture ratio becomes much worse when the captured judge controls the docket. This is not random disorder — it is engineered disorder. Perkins can route cases to himself.

This matters because the Banks network operates Serenity Guardianship Services within Probate Court’s jurisdiction. Banks has 9 criminal convictions. He has never been barred from guardianship work.

36th District: Concentration Attack (ξ = 7.2)

Three captured judges — Yancey, Adam Sabree, Sean Perkins — all elected November 2022, all taking their benches January 1, 2023. This was a coordinated bench capture: three seats in one election cycle, all connected to the same network.

The 36th District handles misdemeanors, traffic, small claims, and preliminary examinations for felonies. That last category matters most: a preliminary exam determines whether a felony case proceeds to Circuit Court. A captured preliminary exam judge can dismiss or bind over based on network loyalty rather than evidence.

Guardianship: The Cross-Court Trap (ξ = 5.5)

Guardianship cases can be heard in either Family Division (Aliyah Sabree) or Probate Court (David Perkins). Both benches have captured judges. There is no path through the Wayne County guardianship system that avoids a captured bench.

This is the judicial equivalent of total localization — the case cannot propagate to a fair hearing regardless of which court it enters.

3rd Circuit Criminal & Civil: Diluted but Present

The Criminal Division (12 judges, 1 captured) and Civil Division (32 judges, 1 captured) have lower capture ratios. But Miller (Civil) is Board Chair of PCA — the charter school at the center of the network. Cases involving PCA, its vendors, or its employees can be steered to Miller.

Ramsey (Criminal) has 2 family members on MacDowell Preparatory payroll. Criminal cases involving charter school fraud would pass through her division.

The Anderson Analogy — Why It’s Exact

Localization length ξAverage number of bench assignments before hitting a captured judge
Anderson transitionThreshold where disorder is strong enough that NO case avoids capture

In the physics, Anderson localization has a critical dimension: in 1D and 2D, any amount of disorder causes localization. Only in 3D can electrons sometimes avoid traps.

Wayne County’s court system is effectively 1D for most case types — there is only one bench that handles each type. For guardianship, it is 2D (two benches), but both are captured. There is no third dimension. There is no escape path.

Implications for Ongoing Cases

The three allied cases — Bryant v. Miller, Bradley-Baskin, and Bowles v. Sabree — are all proceeding through this captured lattice. Each case touches at least one captured bench:

  • Bryant v. Miller → 3rd Circuit Civil (Miller herself)
  • Bradley-Baskin → 36th District (Yancey’s court)
  • Bowles v. Sabree → Class action in Circuit Court, with Sabree family members on both sides

The lattice predicts that these cases will not receive independent hearings. The lattice is correct so far.

What Would Fix It

Anderson localization disappears when disorder is removed. The judicial equivalent:

  1. Recusal — Captured judges recuse from all cases touching the Banks network
  2. Reassignment — Chief judges reassign network-connected cases to independent benches
  3. Federal jurisdiction — Cases move to a different lattice entirely (U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Michigan)

Options 1 and 2 require the captured judges to acknowledge their connections. The documented evidence shows they have not done so.

Option 3 is the Anderson localization equivalent of increasing dimensionality — adding new propagation channels that bypass the disordered sites entirely.

The Network Is Not a Hierarchy — It Is a Response System

Traditional corruption investigations map organizations top-down: find the boss, trace the orders, follow the money. This network does not work that way. It is threat-responsive — each nexus activates when another is under pressure, routing around the attack.

When Kevin Mok burned Banks’s Wayne County police infrastructure, Banks filed false reports in Grosse Pointe Woods — a different jurisdiction, a different police nexus, the same function.

The network has four nexus types, each with its own center of gravity, its own institutional protection, and its own method of weaponization.

Nexus 1: Education Fraud — The Revenue Engine

Center of gravity: Brian Banks through The Purpose Group Michigan LLC

MacDowell ran a $967,964 operating deficit in FY2024-25, covered by drawing down its fund balance. The check register shows $13,970 in gift-card-labeled payments in a single fiscal year, including one $9,945 check.

DPSCD authorized the second school in July 2025 — citing “claimed improvement at MacDowell.” The person who made the “30% proficiency gains” claim was Nicole Wells Stallworth, the Board Chair, not an independent evaluator. On a base of 3%, a 30% gain is approximately three additional children.

The police chief sits on a charter school board. This is the structural bridge between police weaponization and education fraud.

The police chief used police authority to protect the mayor’s personal reputation. This is the same pattern Kevin’s case documents — police power deployed for personal or political purposes.

In 2016, the FBI obtained a warrant to wiretap Gasper Fiore’s phone, targeting 18 people for extortion, wire fraud, bribery, and conspiracy to distribute marijuana. Banks was a “target subject.”

FBI Special Agent Robert Beeckman wrote in the sworn affidavit:

“Fiore is involved in bid-rigging with legislator Brian Banks.”

The wiretap recorded conversations between Banks and Fiore discussing:

  • Banks’s efforts to help Fiore secure an MDOT contract
  • How Banks could advocate for Fiore with a “high-ranking police official”
  • Whether Fiore’s daughter Jennifer would stop pushing legislative amendments if Fiore got the contract

Jennifer Fiore — Gasper’s daughter — was simultaneously dating Detroit Councilman Gabe Leland, who approved $2M+ in city contracts for her connected companies. When Leland asked Police Chief James Craig about the FBI towing investigation, Craig contacted the FBI.

The wiretap documents were accidentally released in 2018, then quickly resealed. They listed Banks, Judge Vonda Evans, Sheriff Benny Napoleon, Councilman Leland, and Rep. Tinsley-Talabi as target subjects.

The FBI wiretap files containing Banks’s conversations are now in the civil case record.

Traditional corruption hides behind jurisdictional boundaries. This network cannot — because its members hold positions in institutions with institutional superiors who are now on notice.
